issues.description: The template Stock.getStockIngredients() returns a List<StockIngredient>, while the solution implements getStockIngredients() to return a StockIngredient[] (the actual private field type). The problem statement also instructs to "add getters for all the private fields," which implies returning the underlying field type. This mismatch between template and solution (and the expectation from the problem statement) can confuse students about the correct getter return type and how to access the stockIngredients field.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Stock.getStockIngredients() signature to return StockIngredient[] (matching the private field) and return this.stockIngredients. Update any code that expects a List to work with the array (or provide an additional helper if a List view is desired). This will align the template with the solution and the problem instruction to add getters for private fields.

issues.description: The getter for the stock's internal collection uses different API shapes across artifacts: the template's Stock.getStockIngredients() returns a List<StockIngredient> while the solution's Stock.getStockIngredients() returns a StockIngredient[] array. This mismatch in the getter signature (same conceptual entity: the stockIngredients collection) can confuse students implementing or using the getter and mapping it to the private field and the problem statement's instructions to add getters for private fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single, consistent getter signature for stockIngredients across template and solution. Prefer returning the same type as the private field (StockIngredient[]), or explicitly document in the problem statement that the getter should return a List<StockIngredient> and update both template and solution to match that choice.
